title: CRLA/263/2010 of MOHD UMAR FAROOQ Vs KULDEEP SINGH

paras.text:

Government Appeal No. 6 of 2011
State of Uttarakhand ... Appellant
Versus
Bheem Singh Bheem Bahadur ... Respondent
Mr. A.S. Gill, Deputy Advocate General, for the State/appellant.
Mr. Nand Gopal Singh and Mr. G.C. Kandpal, Advocates, for the
respondent.
 Date of Judgment: 29.4.2015

Coram: Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
 Hon'ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Per : Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 All the above captioned appeals are being
adjudicated by this single verdict because those all
have arisen out of the same judgment and order dated
19.10.2010 rendered by the 3rd Additional Sessions
Judge, Udham Singh Nagar.
2. Seven accused persons were tried. For
convenience, we may name the accused Babli Man @

3
Virajman as A1, Bheem Bahadur as A2, Satish
Chandra as A3, Prabhu Dayal @ Raju @ Keshav as
A4, Kulwant Singh @ Keti as A5, Sher Bahadur Singh
as A6 and Kuldeep Singh as A7. All these seven
accused persons were tried for the offences under
Section 147, 148, 307 (149), 504, 506, 120B of IPC
pertaining to Crime No. 1146/2005, PS Kichha,
District, Udham Singh Nagar. Out of these seven, A2,
A3 and A4 were also tried for the offence under
Section 25 Arms Act allocating each of them a
separate sessions trial number for the illegal weapon
of assault allegedly recovered from them. Learned
Additional Sessions Judge was of the view that no
charge for any of the offences was found proved
against any of the accused persons beyond reasonable
doubt. So, he passed the order of acquittal of all the
accused persons exonerating them from all the
charges levelled against them. Feeling aggrieved,
Mohd. Umar Farooq, the victim/injured has come up
before us by way of filing the Criminal Appeals
261/2010, 262/2010 and 263/2010, while the
Government has also preferred rest of the appeals as
titled above challenging the acquittal of the accused
persons in Crime No. 1146/2005 as well as the
acquittal of A2, A3 and A4 from the charge of offence
under Section 25 Arms Act in their respective sessions
trial. It can be taken note of that Government has not
preferred any appeal, either by mistake or for some
other reason, against the acquittal of A6 in Crime No.
1146/2005, but such omission on the part of the
Government would not carry any meaning because
acquittal of A6 in Crime No. 1146/2005 has been

4
challenged by the victim Mohd. Umar Farooq by way
of filing the Criminal Appeal No. 261/2010.
3. It is also pertinent to mention that A4
Prabhu Dayal @ Raju @ Keshav died during the
pendency of the appeal on 26.6.2014. His death
certificate is enclosed with the file. So, the appeal
against him stands abated.
4. Now, we come to the factual matrix of the
case and also the evidence available on the record to
appreciate the decision arrived at by the learned
Additional Sessions Judge. Having heard learned
Counsel of all concerned, we notice that the incident
is a diabolical murderous attempt on the brothers duo
by using the lethal weapons. The accused persons
were nurturing the animosity in their hearts against
the victim Mohd. Umar Farooq and his family
members on account of land disputes and litigation.
As per the version countenanced in the first
information report Ex. Ka-1, lodged soon after
inasmuch as within an hour of the incident, the
accused persons always remained in search of some
opportune moment to end the life of the informant
and his brother. Pursuant to their aim and object at
about 4.15 PM on dated 27.5.2005, when Mohd.
Haroon being a pillion rider on a bike driven by his
real brother Mohd. Umar Farooq had just passed the
Kichha Railway Crossing and aheading to the market,
all these accused persons except A1 stopped their
bike. They were all armed with the firearms. A2 and
A3 stopped the bike by holding the handle of the same
from in front. Rest of the accused persons were also
standing with A2 and A3. A5 exhorted rest of the

5
accused persons A4, A6 and A7 not to let off the
brothers duo as they had been found at opportune
moment and they were having 12 bore or 315 bore
country made pistols. So, all of them opened fire
indiscriminately with the aim and object to kill both
the brothers. Mohd. Umar Farooq, who was on the
driving seat, suffered having hit by three fires while
his brother informant Mohd. Haroon quickly fell down
from the bike and could save his life by escaping from
the spot. When the accused were opening the fire, at
that time Mehraj (PW3) and another eyewitness Abdul
Salim (not produced in the Court) were coming from
in front, who saw this violent incident and challenged
the accused persons. On being so challenged and
estimating that they might be apprehended by the
crowd and the witnesses coming from in front, the
accused persons took to their heels threatening of dire
consequences if any legal action is taken against
them. Mohd. Umar Farooq lateron was shifted to
Community Health Centre, Kichha, wherefrom after
the primary treatment, he was referred to Sushila
Tiwari Forest Hospital, Haldwani in the evening of the
same day and from there, finding his condition
serious, he was referred to All India Institute of
Medical Sciences, New Delhi on 29.5.2005 for the
treatment. There the injured Mohd. Umar Farooq
remained admitted for quite a few days and all these
tedious efforts could save his life somehow. This
incident occurred around quarter past four of the day
and the Chick report was recorded at 5 PM of the
same day. So, learned Counsel on behalf of the
respondents/accused has questioned the recording of
this Chick FIR so early. But we are unable to accept

6
this contention for the reason that Kichha Police
Station is about one kilometre away from the place of
occurrence and apart from this, the entire town is
small one. So, the place of incident was not far from
the Community Health Centre as well as the police
station. The accused persons had fled away from the
spot soon after the occurrence. So, it was not
impossible for a young man of 26 years Mohd. Haroon
(PW1), who was the pillion rider, to return at the spot
quickly, lift his injured brother in order to carry him
to the hospital and then go to the police station for
lodging the FIR. Rather, quick reporting of the
incident by way of reducing it into writing dispels the
false implication of the accused persons. There may
be margin of few minutes in making note of the time
in the case diary by the person concerned who
reduced the report in writing, but that is not so
material as to put aside the ocular version of the
witnesses.
5. During the course of investigation, the
Investigation Officer recovered one country made
pistol of 315 bore along with cartridge cover from A4
at his instance, but since he has died, therefore, we
are not inclined to discuss this recovery any further.
In addition to, two country made pistols of 315 bore
along with empty cartridges were also recovered at the
instance of A3 on 10.6.2005. On the same date and
time, another country made pistol of 315 bore was
recovered from A2. So, a common memo of such
recoveries was prepared by the police, which is Ex.
Ka-5.

7
6. Investigation culminated into the
submission of chargesheets against the accused
persons for the offences as have been indicated above.
Resultantly, the charges were levelled accordingly and
the accused persons were put to trial.
7. Before appreciating the evidence of factum,
we would like to take note that in All India Institute of
Medical Sciences, New Delhi, the injured underwent
various radiological examinations, whereupon the
doctor found three foreign metallic objects (bullets)
inside the cavity and by way of undergoing surgical
operations those were got ousted. The radiological
report is Ex. Ka-32. Although the doctor has not been
called to prove such radiological report, but the same
is admissible in evidence because the genuineness of
such report has been endorsed and admitted by the
learned defence counsel on 21.8.2010.

8. In Sushila Tiwari Medical College and
Hospital, too, the injured Mohd. Umar Farooq
underwent the radiological tests wherein the bullets
were visible in the X-ray of his chest and abdomen.
That apart, on account of the bullet injuries, the liver
inside the cavity was found lacerated and bleeding.
This medical report is available as Ex. Ka-7 and has
been proved by PW9 Dr. Ashutosh Sayana. In addition
to, another medical report Ex. Ka-6 has also been
proved which discloses the entry wounds of the
bullets.
9. Now, coming to the ocular version of PW1
Mohd. Haroon, who was a pillion rider and has seen
the occurrence because somehow he could manage to
escape from the spot in order to save his life from the

8
vicious attempt of the assailants, he has proved the
prosecution version as has been disclosed by him in
the FIR in the same manner without any diversion or
deviation. This version of PW1 is in perfect
corroboration of the testimony adduced by Mohd.
Umar Farooq (PW2), who was fatally injured. Over and
above the evidence of these brothers duo, there is an
independent eyewitness account of PW3 Mehraj who
has also corroborated the version of these victim
witnesses while testifying in the witness box. His
ocular version is in the same sequence as has been
deposed by PW1 and PW2. His credibility has also not
been shaken in any manner, nonetheless he was
cross-examined at good length.
10. The grounds of acquittal, which have
been recorded by the learned Trial Judge, are so fickle
in nature as it is difficult for us to be in agreement
with the same, viz. the learned Judge has found that
the registration number of the motorcycle of the victim
which was found lying at the spot was not of a
motorcycle but was of a tractor. However, we feel that
when PW1 and PW2 were put to cross-examination, at
that time this clarification should have been sought
from them by the defence counsel. No attempt in this
regard has been made. Had they been given an
opportunity to clarify or explain this inconsistency,
then it was quite possible for them to offer some
plausible explanation. Learned Trial Judge has failed
to apply his mind in that way. This variation has not
been questioned from the Investigation Officer that he
remained failed to get the clarification of the same
from PW1 and PW2 while recording their statements
under Section 161 CrPC.

9
11. On carefully reading of the impugned
judgment, we feel that the learned Trial Judge has
based his judgment on the minor discrepancies,
inconsistencies and contradictions, viz. one of the
witnesses has said that fire was opened by the
accused persons when Mohd. Umar Farooq had left
the seat of the motorcycle to stand aside. This
discrepancy is immaterial because a person who is
driving the motorcycle, if stopped by the assailants,
may come in the standing posture while still holding
the handle of his bike and being on the driving seat.
Such minor discrepancies should have been ignored
particularly while taking note of the fact that evidence
of these witnesses has been recorded almost after four
years of the incident. So, this long period of gap
inasmuch as 4 years should have been considered
while testing the memory of a witness whose
testimony may suffer with some minor discrepancies
on account of the lapse of this time period.
12. Prowling imaginative doubts in the ocular
testimony of the prosecution witnesses ought not to
be the task of the Court and particularly when the
same is being supported by matching medical
evidence, as the fires were opened by 315 bore
country made pistols and so the three bullets were
found inside the cavity of the victim's body in the
radiological examination.
13. As regards the complicity of A1 the lady
Babli Man is concerned, it has only been stated in the
F.I.R. that almost one hour prior to the incident, rest
of the accused persons were found hatching the
conspiracy in front of the gate of A1 and those were

10
seen as such by PW4 Taushif. This witness PW4 has
deposed that Babli Man was persuading all these
accused persons in slow voice not to let off any of the
brothers duo on that day and this witness Taushif
overheard the voice while passing through that
thoroughfare. This deposition of Taushif is not
believable. So, we discard the same so far as the
complicity of A1 is concerned.
14. Further, as regards the charge under
Section 25 Arms Act against A2 and A3 is concerned,
the recovery memo Ex. Ka-5 was prepared because
these weapons were recovered at their own instance.
Their signatures are present on the recovery memo.
When these accused A2 and A3 were rendered an
opportunity to explain in their statement under
Section 313 CrPC, they had not even denied their
respective signatures on the recovery memo despite
being asked and they gave an evasive reply that
"documents have wrongly been produced".
15. In view of what has been discussed above,
we are of the considered opinion that the prosecution
has proved all the charges against the accused
persons except Babli Man (A1) beyond reasonable
doubt and this way learned Additional Sessions Judge
remained failed to appreciate the verity of the
formidable evidence available on the record.
Consequently, we set aside the impugned judgment
dated 19.10.2010 and allow all these appeals
captioned above. We record the conviction of all the
accused persons A2, A3, A5, A6 and A7, except that of
Babli Man (A1), for the offences under Section 147,

11
148, 307 (149), 504, 506, 120B IPC and sentence
them as under:
(i) For the offence of Section 147 IPC, each
one of the convicts will undergo six
months' rigorous imprisonment.
(ii) For the offence of Section 148 IPC, each
one of the convicts will undergo one
year's rigorous imprisonment.
(iii) For the offence of Section 307 (149) IPC,
each one of the convicts will undergo five
year's rigorous imprisonment and will
pay fine of rupees five thousand each. In
default of payment of such fine, every
defaulter convict will further undergo six
months' imprisonment.
(iv) For the offence of Section 504 IPC, each
one of the convicts will undergo six
months' rigorous imprisonment.
(v) For the offence of Section 506/120B IPC,
each one of the convicts will undergo one
year's imprisonment.
All the sentences shall run concurrently.
16. Bheem Bahadur (A2) and Satish Chandra
(A3) are also convicted for the offence under Section
25 Arms Act and both of them are sentenced for a
term of three years' imprisonment along with fine of
rupees two thousand each. In default of payment of
such fine, they will undergo three months'
imprisonment in addition. This sentence will also run
concurrently along with other sentences awarded for
the offences in Crime No. 1146/2005. It is hereby
made clear that the period already undergone by any

12
of the convicts hereinbefore shall be adjusted in their
respective sentences awarded by this Court.
18. All the convicts shall be taken into custody
forthwith to serve out the sentence. A copy of this
judgment and order be sent to the trial court to
ensure its compliance. Let the lower court record be
sent back.
(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (Alok Singh, J.)
 Prabodh
